title: What VPSF means
question: What is Value Per Square Foot?
body: VPSF is a home-performance score out of 1,000, based on the information available for one home.

sections.heading: What it covers
sections.text: Seven pillars span energy, water, health, resilience, materials, financial risk, and community and mobility.

sections.heading: What it does not measure
sections.text: It is not a dollar-per-square-foot appraisal, certification, resale estimate, or promise of future value.

title: How the calculator works
question: How does the VPSF calculator work?
body: Enter an address, then review and correct what the calculator finds.

sections.heading: Add details
sections.text: Record key systems. Saved homes may load archived facts; new scans may use public records and location-risk data.

sections.heading: See results
sections.text: Generate VPSF Score rates available evidence across seven pillars. My Scores opens results; Menu links to recommendations, learning, products, and sharing.

sections.heading: Keep in mind
sections.text: Better verified details make the report more useful, but do not guarantee a higher score.

title: Finding relevant products
question: Where can I get more information on the best products to raise my home's VPSF score?
body: Recommended Products shows options linked to the home's improvement opportunities.

sections.heading: Explore
sections.text: From Recommendations, use Product Options to compare categories. Learn More explains the building science behind an upgrade.

sections.heading: Check fit
sections.text: A listing alone adds no points. Ask a qualified professional about fit, local requirements, pricing, and proof of installation and performance.

title: Correcting or adding home details
question: What if a home detail is missing or wrong?
body: On Review & Confirm, use Edit/Add Details to fix missing or incorrect facts.

sections.heading: Check systems
sections.text: Record known equipment type and age, including HVAC, water heating, roofing, ventilation, solar, and storage. Use All Home Specs for more.

sections.heading: Verify
sections.text: Confirm the address and support changes with permits, labels, invoices, photos, or inspections. Added details are saved for later visits.

title: Performance expectations
question: Do you guarantee performance increases?
body: No. VPSF estimates are not a guarantee of real-world performance or score gains.

sections.heading: Why results vary
sections.text: Product choice, design, installation, maintenance, and other construction details can affect performance.

sections.heading: Our basis
sections.text: The model draws on decades of building-science experience, not AI. Sound building science can improve a property; verify actual performance after improvements.

title: Address and public records
body: The address connects a home to saved scans, public records, climate context, and hazard layers.

sections.heading: Check the match
sections.text: Street and state abbreviations are normalized, but confirm the ZIP and property details before scoring.

sections.heading: Know the gaps
sections.text: Public records may show permits and basic facts. They rarely prove equipment efficiency, ventilation, water fixtures, or resilience upgrades.

title: Documenting key systems
body: Key Systems records major features that affect home performance.

sections.heading: Include
sections.text: Heating and cooling, water heating, roof, ventilation, solar, and battery storage, with type, age, or capacity when known.

sections.heading: Unknowns
sections.text: Use All Home Specs for additional measures. Leave unknown details blank until you can verify them; missing information is not proof of an upgrade.

title: What counts as evidence
body: Use documents or clear photos to back up a home feature.

sections.heading: Useful proof
sections.text: Labels identify models; invoices show installation dates. Permits, inspection reports, and specification sheets add context.

sections.heading: Resolve conflicts
sections.text: Check extracted details. If a public record conflicts with the home, use verified current conditions and keep the source for later review.

title: Reading the VPSF score
body: The VPSF total adds seven pillar scores, with 1,000 points available in the current model.

sections.heading: Read the detail
sections.text: The overview shows the total and label. Pillar pages show strengths, missing evidence, and upgrade opportunities.

sections.heading: Avoid confusion
sections.text: A percentage of available points is not a market percentile. The report is not a certification, insurance quote, or savings guarantee.

title: The seven scoring pillars
body: Each pillar measures a different part of home performance and has its own point maximum.

sections.heading: Energy
sections.text: Efficiency, electrification, and energy exposure.

sections.heading: Water
sections.text: Conservation and water-damage risk.

sections.heading: Health
sections.text: Indoor conditions, including ventilation and moisture.

sections.heading: Resilience
sections.text: Hazards and the home's ability to withstand them.

sections.heading: Carbon & Materials
sections.text: Material impacts and documentation.

sections.heading: Financial Risk
sections.text: Ownership-cost exposure.

sections.heading: Community & Mobility
sections.text: Surrounding context and transportation.

sections.heading: Where to look
sections.text: Menu has general definitions; My Scores shows the assessed home's results.

title: How location affects the report
body: Location sets climate and hazard context for the report.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text: When coordinates are available, public flood and wildfire layers may be used.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: These area-level signals can be missing or imprecise; they do not replace a site inspection. After correcting an address, review its risk context again.

sections.heading: Planning
sections.text: Let local hazards guide resilience upgrades.

title: Using recommendations
body: Recommendations target weaknesses in the current home record.

sections.heading: Explore
sections.text: Each includes a summary, Learn More for building science, and Product Options for relevant categories.

sections.heading: Use impact points
sections.text: Points are model estimates, not guaranteed gains or savings. Compare options with equipment, climate, budget, and documentation.

sections.heading: Recheck
sections.text: After work, update the saved home and score it again.

title: Learning the building science
body: Learn More explains why an upgrade matters and how it works.

sections.heading: Watch or read
sections.text: Some topics have a short video; written details remain available. Find topics from recommendations or Building Science Basics in Menu.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.text: Use the guide to question contractors, then verify product and installation fit for this home.

title: Finding Green Builder know-how
body: Know-How Archives collect Green Builder Media articles by pillar.

sections.heading: Browse
sections.text: Open them from Building Science Basics or Key Takeaway. Individual articles use a clean reader; collections show linked lists.

sections.heading: Use with care
sections.text: Articles offer background, not a project-specific design, inspection, or local code review.

title: Planning a path to 700
body: Path to 700 organizes upgrades toward the High Performance threshold.

sections.heading: Prioritize
sections.text: Start with missing or weak systems, then choose work suited to the home's climate and condition.

sections.heading: Check progress
sections.text: Keep installation and performance proof, update the saved home, and recalculate. Displayed points are estimates, not promises.

title: Understanding future cost exposure
body: Future Cost Exposure compares ownership risks such as aging systems, utilities, maintenance, and insurance.

sections.heading: Use it
sections.text: Check equipment condition, local prices, and climate hazards before deciding what to replace.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: It is not a personal quote or bill forecast. VPSF points are separate from real-world dollars.

title: Using the VPSF Report Card
body: The Report Card summarizes the address, total, performance label, and seven pillar scores.

sections.heading: Before sharing
sections.text: Check for missing or incorrect details.

sections.heading: Export
sections.text: Download the single-page PDF or use Share Report. It is not a certified label, appraisal, market percentile, or savings guarantee.

title: Sharing your score
body: Share Your Score presents a home's strengths, improvement opportunities, and supporting information.

sections.heading: Review first
sections.text: Check the address, photos, score, and claims. Keep system and upgrade records current.

sections.heading: Portable summary
sections.text: Use the VPSF Report Card for a downloadable score summary.

title: Data, privacy, and limits
body: VPSF combines your entries with available public or partner data and saves property details for later scans.

sections.heading: Your choice
sections.text: Add only documents and personal details you are comfortable storing.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Public records can be incomplete. Confirm important decisions with a professional; a score does not replace an inspection, audit, underwriting, or appraisal.
